name: architecture-errors
text: Errors: 422 input · 404 missing · commit conflict: rollback, then 200 or 409. No live GAF/AI call.

preview: A · Snapshot | B · CLI | C · Validate | D · Upsert | E · Score | F · Persist

text:
SPEAKING SCRIPT
Read the numbered runtime path from left to right across the top, then right to left across the bottom. React components issue typed HTTP calls through lib/api.ts. Next.js forwards /api/v1 to Flask. Routes use integer path conversion and Pydantic query/body schemas where applicable; save has no request body. Services apply read and save rules. Queries and SQLAlchemy models perform joined reads or stage Lead inserts. PostgreSQL enforces unique keys at commit. After a new save, expire_all invalidates stale ORM state before prospect_detail reloads and constructs the Pydantic response. Reads skip this save-only expiration. The route serializes with model_dump and jsonify; the client unwraps success/error results. React renders the response. A successful Prospects save starts list and statistics GETs independently. Errors can short-circuit the numbered success path: invalid input returns 422 before service/database work, missing records return 404, and IntegrityError triggers rollback followed by an existing-save 200 or other-listing 409. Network failure after commit remains ambiguous; retry can recover the saved lead. The setup row is an explicit CLI operation, not a request-time dependency or background job: recorded JSON, import-snapshot, load_snapshot validation and normalization, source upsert/commit, rescore imported IDs with score_prospect, then score upsert/commit. Source and scores have separate commit boundaries. No live GAF or AI call occurs.

GAF blocks automated HTTP clients, so we could not scrape from the server. We used Claude in Chrome inside a normal Chrome session. First we proved that the search really filters by ZIP code. title: All prospects or only high scores?

name: title
text: All prospects or only high scores?

name: note
text: Score explains priority; the representative decides.

SPEAKING SCRIPT
We keep every listing. All 409 prospects are stored and scored, at every tier. The score explains priority; it does not decide what is stored, because a low score can come from missing data rather than a poor fit. A lead is any prospect that a representative saves, at any tier, and only one lead per company. Filters, not deletion, hide what a rep does not want to see.
